question: In August 2025, DRDO tested 'Sudarshan Chakra' project related to _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Air Defence Laser System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DRDO** (Defence Research and Development Organisation) tested the 'Sudarshan Chakra' project in **August 2025**. The project is related to the development of **Air Defence Laser Systems**.
 
• The **Air Defence Laser System** is a cutting-edge technology designed to counter aerial threats such as **drones, missiles, and aircraft**.
 
• Laser-based air defence systems use **directed energy weapons** to neutralize threats by either damaging or disrupting their operational capabilities.
 
• This system provides **high precision and rapid response** capabilities, making it an essential component of modern air defence mechanisms.
 
• The 'Sudarshan Chakra' project reflects India's commitment to **strengthening its defence technology** and achieving self-reliance in military systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Air Defence Laser Systems:**

 
 
• These systems use **high-energy lasers** to target and neutralize incoming threats.
 
• The lasers operate at the speed of light, ensuring **instantaneous action** against fast-moving targets.
 
• They are capable of targeting threats with **precision**, minimizing collateral damage.
 
• Laser systems have a lower operational cost compared to traditional missile defence systems as they rely on **electric power** rather than expensive ammunition.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Laser-based Defence Systems:**
 
 
• Used to counter **unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)** and drones.
 
• Protects strategic installations from **missile attacks**.
 
• Supports integrated air defence systems by providing a layer of **.
 
• Effective in neutralizing swarm attacks where multiple small drones or UAVs are deployed simultaneously.
 
 
 
• Global Examples of Laser Defence Systems:**
 
 
• The United States has developed systems such as the **Laser Weapon System (LaWS)**, which is deployed on naval ships.
 
• Israel's **Iron Beam** is a short-range laser-based air defence system designed to complement its Iron Dome.
 
• China is also working on laser-based defence technologies for its military applications.
 
 
 
• **Role of DRDO:**
 
 
• DRDO is India’s premier agency for developing advanced military technologies such as **missile systems, electronic warfare systems, and directed energy weapons**.
 
• The 'Sudarshan Chakra' project aligns with DRDO's vision to achieve **indigenization of defence technologies**.
 
• It contributes to enhancing India’s **national security** and reducing dependency on foreign defence systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference Between Traditional and Laser-based Air Defence Systems:**

 
 
• Traditional systems rely on **missiles or projectiles**, which have a limited supply and higher operational costs.
 
• Laser systems use **directed energy**, offering unlimited usage as long as power is available.
 
• Laser-based systems provide **silent operations** and are harder to detect compared to traditional systems.
 
 
 
• **Future of Laser Defence Systems:**
 
 
• Expected to play a critical role in countering threats from **hypersonic weapons**.
 
• Will be increasingly integrated into **multi-layered defence frameworks**.
 
• Ongoing research focuses on enhancing **power output and range** to tackle more advanced threats effectively.
